notes.title: Try Arranger and keep your progress!
notes.content:
Hello Arrangers!

A few fun updates for you:

Y’all asked for it, and our demo is back online! It also now allows you to carry over your save to the full game - so enjoy the first hour of the adventure, and then buy the full game to keep going. The demo is also [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2916350/Arranger_A_RolePuzzling_Adventure_Demo/]listed on its own page now[/url], which means you can leave a review on it! Or send it to a friend! Please and thank you.

Our artist David recently worked on a very entertaining video about our art team and how it all came together. So check that out!
[previewyoutube=YbbpStG5Ms0;full][/previewyoutube]
Our composer Tomas put together a beautiful video about one of his recording sessions for the game’s soundtrack. Check that out too!
[previewyoutube=Ywn4HqJ5sjQ;full][/previewyoutube]
We’re currently exploring things like a physical version of the game, a vinyl release of the soundtrack, and maybe more. If you’re excited about those things - or just want to report a bug - let us know! In our Steam forums, via Twitter, or at hello@arranger.quest.

Thanks!

notes.title: Arranger is OUT NOW!
notes.content:
That’s right: Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure is out! Check out our launch trailer!

[previewyoutube=s3RYrlFwEW8;full]https://youtu.be/s3RYrlFwEW8
[/previewyoutube]
You can grab Arranger for $19.99, or in a neat bundle with our gorgeous soundtrack - composed by Tomas Batista - for $29.99. We also have a limited-time launch sale for 10% off both!

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/43481/


And if you’ve never played the other charming puzzle adventure game Carto (also written by our writer Nick Suttner), you can buy them both together in a new discounted bundle (or get Arranger discounted if you already own Carto!).

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/43571/Arranger__Carto_game_bundle/

It’s been a long journey for us, but so we’re proud to share Jemma and her world with you! We packed it full of interesting puzzles, charming characters, gorgeous art, stirring music, and a sweet story about self-discovery. We hope you love it!

If you have any questions, thoughts, hopes, or dreams, let us know at hello@arranger.quest

Happy puzzling!

Best,

Furniture & Mattress

notes.title: Arranger launches on July 25th + demo live now!
notes.content:
Hello, aspiring Arrangers!

We just announced some big news at Summer Games Fest:
Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure will be launching on July 25th for $19.99!

Check out our brand-new trailer: 
[previewyoutube=z6DYP22p9dg;full]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z6DYP22p9dg[/previewyoutube]
Also, we have a playable demo live now! Check it out!
It’s the first hour or so of the game, as Jemma spends one last, slightly awkward day in her hometown before heading out into the Wilderness beyond. You’ll get a taste of our nice clicky mechanics, our charming, weirdo world, and maybe even a boss!

We’re super happy with how the game turned out, and so grateful that you’re interested in our li’l role-puzzler. If you haven’t yet, give it a wishlist!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2596420/Arranger_A_RolePuzzling_Adventure/

The game is all done, we’re just putting on the finishing touches and preparing for our launch. We’ll also be going on a little tour with the game - if you’ll be at Tribeca in NYC, BIG Festival in Brazil, or BitSummit in Kyoto, come say hello!

We’ll be back with more news soon, but in the meantime, why not subscribe to our newsletter over at [url=arranger.quest]arranger.quest[/url]? It’s like this, but with more seeeeecrets. 

All the best,

Furniture & Mattress

notes.title: Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure is the debut game from former Braid, Carto and Ethereal devs
notes.content:
This week's Nintendo Direct was stuffed full of games that will also be making their way to PC over the next few months, but the one I haven't been able to stop thinking about is the newly-announced Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure. It's the debut game from a team of indie devs that include Braid artist David Hellman, Carto writer Nick Suttner and Ethereal designer Nicolás Recabarren, and they've also partnered with composer Tomás Batista, who did the music for both Ethereal and Martian colony builder Per Aspera. It's a pretty stacked line-up as these things go, but it's Arranger's world of constantly shifting sliding tiles that's really piqued my curiosity. Come and watch the lovely announcement trailer below and see what I mean.
